title: Algebraic presentation of pro-etale internal module inverse image
statement: For any morphism f:X to Y of schemes in universe u, commutative monoid objects R and S in abelian sheaves in universe u+1 on their respective pro-etale sites, and a monoid isomorphism rho:S to f*R, let L be set-valued inverse image constructed as sheafification after left Kan extension along the opposite of pro-etale base change. Using [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], there exists an AlgebraicInverseImageOfUniverses structure [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image] over L, from the section ring of R to that of S, whose module functor is naturally isomorphic to the inverse source section-module equivalence followed by Mod.mapModComap rho and the target section-module equivalence. Both rings and modules have universe u+1. No flatness assumption or flatness conclusion occurs in this identification.

proof.text: For the base-change functor U, both inverse images are inclusion into presheaves followed by U.op.lan and sheafification. Its costructured-arrow categories are filtered, since U is representably flat. The abelian forgetful functor preserves filtered colimits (shrink the morphism universe when necessary), giving a natural comparison of the two Kan extensions. It also preserves sheafification. Compose these comparisons to identify the underlying set sheaf of abelian inverse image with L applied to the underlying set sheaf. These data are constructed in the module as pullbackForgetIso. The lemma pullbackForgetIso_unit_hom proves compatibility with adjunction units from the inverse Kan comparison factorization and sheafComposeNatTrans_fac.

Apply this comparison to R and compose with the inverse of rho on underlying sheaves; insert the canonical equal-universe ULift identifications. This constructs ringUnderlying. Define the module functor to be exactly inverse section equivalence, internal inverse image with coefficient restriction, and target section equivalence. The same comparison and the counit of the section equivalence construct moduleUnderlying naturally on this functor. The concrete private constructions sectionRingPullbackIso and sectionModulePullbackIso implement these isomorphisms without sorry.

For each of the seven operation graph fields, form the two maps from L(T) to the target underlying set sheaf and transpose through the set-sheaf adjunction. Naturality and pullbackForgetIso_unit_hom identify their transposes with the source maps followed by the abelian adjunction unit and the inverse coefficient isomorphism. The unit preserves addition and zero because its components are additive; it preserves multiplication and one by the monoidal adjunction unit homomorphism property, evaluated using the tensor and unit formulas for pushforward. The existing sectionRingPullback_add_graph, sectionRingPullback_mul_graph and sectionRingPullback_nat_graph give all four ring fields. For modules, sectionModulePullbackIso_inv_factor and sectionModulePullbackIso_inv_apply express the comparison as the inverse source section-equivalence counit followed by the abelian pullback comparison and canonical universe lifts. The linear counit transports source addition and zero, so pullback_add_graph and pullback_zero_graph give moduleAdd and moduleZero. For the scalar field, sectionModuleCounit_smul supplies the counit scalar equation, and section_comap_smul identifies the section action after restriction of scalars. Apply sectionModuleFunctor to the unit of Adjunction.mapModAdjunction: the resulting linear maps preserve scalar multiplication. Rewrite the target action with section_comap_smul and pushforward_section_smul, then use rho followed by its inverse to obtain inverseImageSectionModuleUnit_smul for the coefficient identification. The lemma sectionModulePullbackIso_transpose identifies the module comparison's transpose with this unit composed with the linear section-equivalence counit. Use moduleSMulSections to form the target scalar graph as a morphism. Transposition, the source graph equation, counit linearity and inverseImageSectionModuleUnit_smul prove equality of its two maps. Evaluate at every target section and apply ULift.down. Assemble the seven proved fields and choose the composite section-module functor itself with the identity comparison isomorphism. All constructions and identities are valid for zero rings/modules and empty sites.

theorem exists_sectionModuleAlgebraicInverseImage {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (R : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology Y) Ab.{u + 1}) [MonObj R] [IsCommMonObj R]
    (S : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) [MonObj S] [IsCommMonObj S]
    (ρ : S ⟶ (f)^*[Ab.{u + 1}].obj R) [IsMonHom ρ] [IsIso ρ] :
    let L := Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback
      (MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @WeaklyEtale ⊤ f) (Type (u + 1))
      (Scheme.ProEt.topology Y) (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
    ∃ I : SheafOfModules.AlgebraicInverseImageOfUniverses.{u + 1, u, u + 1, u, u + 1, u + 1} L
        (InternalAbelianSheafModule.sectionRingSheaf.{u + 1, u + 1, u}
          (Scheme.ProEt.topology Y) R)
        (InternalAbelianSheafModule.sectionRingSheaf.{u + 1, u + 1, u}
          (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) S),
      Nonempty
        ((InternalAbelianSheafModule.sectionModuleEquivalence.{u + 1, u + 1, u}
            (Scheme.ProEt.topology Y) R).inverse ⋙ Mod.mapModComap ρ ⋙
          (InternalAbelianSheafModule.sectionModuleEquivalence.{u + 1, u + 1, u}
            (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) S).functor ≅ I.modules)
